entities.evidence: The verse gives Noah’s age at the flood, identifying him as Lamech’s son. The source tag agrees.

name_review_base.evidence: The verse gives Noah’s age at the flood, identifying him as Lamech’s son. The source tag agrees.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: בֶּן שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה gives Noah’s age. He was six hundred years old when the flood came upon the earth.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the masculine singular personal name נֹחַ.

analysis.evidence: בֶּן introduces שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, “six hundred years,” giving Noah’s age when the flood came.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: one marked by an age, a quality or a fate (idiom)

analysis.evidence: שֵׁשׁ counts מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’. The age expression בֶּן שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה gives Noah’s age as six hundred years.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: six as the multiplier in six hundred

analysis.evidence: In שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שֵׁשׁ counts six units of a hundred. The phrase gives Noah’s age as six hundred years.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In בֶּן שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שָׁנָה supplies the unit in the age expression. Noah was six hundred years old when the flood came.

draft.change: Link this occurrence to the existing flood sense of מַבּוּל at word index 0. The current article already cites Genesis 7:6 as defining evidence.
draft.definition: An inundation in which rising waters cover the land.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:6 describes הַמַּבּוּל as מַיִם עַל הָאָרֶץ, “water upon the earth.”

analysis.evidence: הַמַּבּוּל is the subject of the masculine singular verb הָיָה. The phrase מַיִם עַל הָאָרֶץ, “water upon the earth,” identifies it as the flood announced in Genesis 6:17.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ “and” and the definite article הַ “the” precede the masculine singular absolute common noun מַבּוּל. The article doubles the noun’s initial מ.
analysis.sense: The flood that covered the earth in Noah’s day.

analysis.evidence: הָיָה agrees with the masculine singular subject הַמַּבּוּל, “the flood.” The clause dates the event to Noah’s six hundredth year of life as reckoned by his stated age of six hundred: the flood came, with water over the earth (מַיִם עַל הָאָרֶץ).
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

draft.change: Add Genesis 9:15 as an example of the existing sense a-body-or-flow.
draft.definition: A body or flow of water, including waters that rise in a flood.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:15 calls the waters הַמַּיִם and the flood they could become מַבּוּל.

analysis.evidence: מַיִם identifies the waters of הַמַּבּוּל, the flood already present in this verse. עַל הָאָרֶץ locates those waters on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: A body of water capable of becoming a flood.

analysis.evidence: In מַיִם עַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל introduces הָאָרֶץ and locates the floodwaters on the earth.
מַיִם עַל הָאָרֶץ places the floodwaters “upon the earth.” The phrase describes the earth as a whole, with no particular territory in view.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute, in pausal form.
